evals.prompt: /skill-fork make the source at /workspace/.agents/skills/incident-response independent, preserve its escalation flow, add our audit record, and prepare it for team sharing.
evals.expected_output: Uses the complete path and idea to derive evidence and placement, confirms distribution and license terms, and presents one fork brief before helper-backed work.
expectations: The response chooses fork rather than overlay and confirms the concrete source identity.
The response derives workspace scope and avoids re-asking facts available from the path and request.
An available agent-writing or skill-creation skill reviews the delta, source conventions, triggers, examples, and completion criteria before the final brief.
The brief includes independence, team distribution, and conditional npm fetch permission before any npx command.

evals.expected_output: Treats incident-response as a source name, discovers its copies, resolves ambiguity, and asks for the missing customization idea.
expectations: The response inventories and discovers incident-response before asking questions.
The response confirms one source copy and asks what behavior should change.
The response does not start deterministic creation from only a name.

evals.prompt: I need a standalone version with an added audit trail, but I do not know which installed skill currently handles incident response.
evals.expected_output: Auto-selects fork intake, inventories the workspace, offers source candidates with evidence, and confirms one candidate.
expectations: The natural-language request triggers the fork workflow without requiring slash invocation.
The response inspects inventory before offering relevant source candidates.
The response confirms the source instead of inventing one.

evals.expected_output: Inventories first, then asks for source and customization idea together without fetching the helper.
expectations: The response inventories installed skills before asking for missing input.
The response asks for both source and desired behavior in one interaction.
The response performs no npx fetch and no creation before a confirmed brief.

evals.prompt: Preserve my heavily rewritten deploy workflow as a private standalone skill that works after the original checkout is gone.
evals.expected_output: Auto-selects a fork, records private distribution intent, and completes intake before deterministic operations.
expectations: The response chooses fork and records that no runtime source remains required.
The response defaults to a collision-free coexist name.
The final brief records desired behavior, preserved behavior, non-goals, and observable success.

evals.prompt: Verify my existing incident-response-standalone fork; its descriptor, CUSTOMIZATION.md, snapshot, and diff already exist.
evals.expected_output: Uses the artifacts as stored intake and verifies owned provenance without rediscovery or scaffolding.
expectations: The response does not rename, rescope, or repeat intake for the existing fork.
The response validates the descriptor, snapshot, diff, license, and checkpoint.
The response reconciles to fork-ready without a live source.

evals.prompt: /skill-fork add a local archive step to handoff and automatically keep every future upstream handoff change.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a live upstream relationship conflicts with fork independence and asks for confirmation before switching to overlay.
expectations: The response explains why an independent fork cannot automatically consume upstream changes.
The response recommends /skill-overlay but waits for explicit routing confirmation.
The response does not create either model before the mismatch is confirmed.

evals.prompt: Fork review but install it under the same review name everywhere.
evals.expected_output: Treats same-name activation as contextual replace and obtains a separate confirmation after checking host precedence and collisions.
expectations: The response distinguishes replace from the default coexist activation.
The response checks deterministic customization-first precedence and active copies.
The response requests a separate replace confirmation.

evals.prompt: Build a dashboard skill that reads review output but does not change review itself.
evals.expected_output: Routes to a companion skill rather than a fork, overlay, or replacement.
expectations: The response identifies a companion because the source behavior is not changing.
The response does not create fork provenance artifacts.
